rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and the provided 4AA label, but it overstates certainty from this single image: hatching/herniation and a clearly continuous cohesive TE are not convincingly visible, and some described details (distinct borders, vesicular debris interpretation) are somewhat inferred.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, low oocyte yield, prior live birth, endometrial thickness, male factor, paternal age, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a plausible prognosis tied to embryo grade and patient factors. Minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments and a few assumptions not directly supported by the case data.

Largely aligned with standard IVF practice: SET for a top-quality day-5 blastocyst, appropriate counseling, and reasonable discussion of protocol review and selective use of PGT-A. Small deviations include overconfident endorsement of some adjuncts and speculative protocol changes without full cycle details.
Provides clear, practical next steps for the current transfer and contingency planning, including luteal support, follow-up timing, counseling, and future stimulation/sperm evaluation considerations.
